about: MCPs and skills we list in the catalog but don't build: open-source ones (with their repo and licence) and hosted ones from their makers. Always public, never packaged by us: the install plan hands out `install.source`. Admins add one here (or through the admin API, which wins). Skills point at them from their `## First: check the MCPs` table. See apps/mediamake/docs/catalog-releases.md.

items.title: ElevenLabs
items.summary: Sound effects, speech, voices, transcription and audio isolation from ElevenLabs, as files on your computer. The official open-source MCP server, and the key MediaMake's npm run transcribe uses for timed words.

env.name: ELEVENLABS_API_KEY
env.description: Your ElevenLabs API key. At the link (Developers > API Keys) create one: Restrict Key is on by default, so turn it off or allow Speech to Text, Text to Speech, Sound Effects, Voices and User. Copy it at once (shown only once). MediaMake's npm run transcribe reads it here too.

env.name: ELEVENLABS_MCP_BASE_PATH
env.description: The folder it may read input files from and saves to by default (~/Desktop when unset). Set it to your home folder so it can use files in your projects.

install.notes: Needs an ElevenLabs account (the free tier has 10,000 credits a month) and uv. Every generation spends credits.

items.title: ElevenLabs connector
items.summary: ElevenLabs' hosted connector from Claude's directory: speech, voices and transcription with every word's start and end, plus ElevenAgents voice agents. Signs in with your ElevenLabs account: nothing to install, no key. The alternative to the ElevenLabs MCP where nothing local runs (the Claude web and phone apps).

source.name: elevenlabs-connector
setup: Only when the ElevenLabs MCP can't run here (the Claude web or phone app): sign in with your ElevenLabs account and click Allow. It is ready when Claude has the creative_transcribe_audio tool.

install.notes: Hosted by ElevenLabs: nothing runs on your computer and it can't read your files, so a song on your computer goes in through its file picker widget, and every result (a transcription, a voice, a sound effect) is a flow run to download from. No music. Needs an ElevenLabs account; every generation spends credits. On a computer the ElevenLabs MCP (an API key, files straight on the computer, no widget) comes first.

items.title: fal
items.summary: Image, video and audio models on fal (Nano Banana, upscalers, image-to-video, cutouts), hosted by fal.

install.notes: Needs a fal account with credits: every image or video it makes is paid.

items.title: Blender
items.summary: Build, import and render 3D scenes in Blender from Claude. Open source, through a Blender add-on.

source.name: blender
setup: Install its Blender add-on: `uvx mcp-for-blender install-addon`.

Ask them to open Blender, go to Edit → Preferences → Add-ons and turn on Interface: MCP for Blender. The add-on starts its server when Blender opens (press N in the 3D viewport → MCP for Blender tab → Start MCP Server if it isn't running).

install.notes: Needs Blender 3.0 or newer and uv. Blender has to be open, with the add-on's server running, whenever Claude uses it.

items.title: Gemini
items.summary: Google's Gemini 3 models from Claude: image generation and editing up to 4K (Nano Banana Pro), Veo video, speech with 30 voices, Google Search with citations, deep research, YouTube and document analysis, code execution and a second opinion from Gemini Pro or Flash. Open source, runs on your computer with a Google AI Studio key.

env.name: GEMINI_API_KEY
env.description: Your Google Gemini API key from Google AI Studio (Get API key > Create API key; free, takes seconds). The server checks it when it starts, so a wrong key stops it.

env.name: GEMINI_OUTPUT_DIR
env.description: The folder its images, videos and audio are saved to (~/.config/gemini-mcp/output/<folder hash> when unset). With MediaMake's media library set up, point it at the library's inbox (~/Downloads/_INBOX/gemini) so `media ingest` files what it makes.

env.name: GEMINI_TOOL_PRESET
env.description: Which of its 37 tools to load, to keep Claude's context small: minimal, text, image, research, media or full (all 18 tool groups, the default). GEMINI_ENABLED_TOOLS adds tool groups to a preset, e.g. search,image-gen.

install.notes: Needs Node 18 or newer (npx comes with it) and a Google AI Studio API key; the free tier works but is rate-limited (429s: set GEMINI_MODEL=gemini-3-flash-preview or move to a paid plan). Images, video, speech and research spend your Google API quota. Also installs the gcli command (npm install -g @rlabs-inc/gemini-mcp) for the same tools from a terminal.

items.title: Figcraft
items.summary: An open-source design editor (frames, text, images, auto layout, components) that Claude drives from its MCP server and command line: it builds and edits simple layouts such as banners, thumbnails, social posts and pitch decks as .figcraft files, exports them as PNG, JPG, SVG or PDF, and opens them in the FigCraft app for you to change anything by hand. MediaMake's thumbnails use it for their final edit. Free, local, no account.

source.name: figcraft

install: Get figcraft-cli from the latest release at https://github.com/storytold/figcraft/releases/latest, for this computer:
On a Mac: figcraft-cli-<version>-macos-universal.zip (signed and notarized); unzip it and put figcraft-cli in ~/.local/bin.

On Windows: the FigCraft app, figcraft-<version>-windows-x64.msi (windows-arm64 on an ARM computer); figcraft-cli.exe comes with it, in its folder (ArtCraft\FigCraft under Program Files, or under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs when installed for one account).
On Linux: the AppImage runs it as `FigCraft.AppImage cli`; put a figcraft-cli script in ~/.local/bin that runs `<path>/FigCraft.AppImage cli "$@"`.
Check: `figcraft-cli --version` (by its full path when its folder isn't on the PATH).

setup: For editing by hand, the FigCraft app from the same release (on a Mac figcraft-<version>-macos-universal.dmg; on Windows it came with figcraft-cli). Started as `figcraft --control 7979`, a second server, `figcraft-cli mcp --attach 7979`, lets Claude change the open window while you watch.

install.notes: Early alpha, by its makers' own account. Runs on your computer and needs no account or key; it reaches the network only when you share a file from the app. Text uses the fonts installed on the computer plus ones a session loads (text.loadFont), so install a design's fonts before opening it in the app. The use-figcraft skill says how Claude builds, checks and exports a layout with it.

items.title: Soundcraft
items.summary: An open-source digital audio workstation (tracks, a mixer with plugins, sends, buses and automation, MIDI and built-in instruments, offline processing, bounce) that Claude drives from its MCP server and command line with no window: it mixes a song from its stems, masters to a loudness target, edits and converts audio, and saves .scraft sessions that open in the SoundCraft app for you to mix by hand. Free, local, no account.

source.name: soundcraft

install: Get soundcraft-cli from the latest release at https://github.com/storytold/soundcraft/releases/latest, for this computer, and check it against the release's SHA256SUMS.txt:
On a Mac: soundcraft-cli-<version>-macos-universal.zip (signed and notarized); unzip it and put soundcraft-cli in ~/.local/bin.
On Windows: the SoundCraft app, soundcraft-<version>-windows-x64.msi (windows-arm64 on an ARM computer); soundcraft-cli.exe comes with it, in its folder.
On Linux: soundcraft-<version>-linux-x86_64.tar.gz (aarch64 on ARM) carries soundcraft-cli; put it in ~/.local/bin.
Check: `soundcraft-cli --version` (by its full path when its folder isn't on the PATH).

setup: For mixing by hand and for listening, the SoundCraft app from the same release (on a Mac soundcraft-<version>-macos-universal.dmg). Started as `soundcraft --control 7801`, a second server, `soundcraft-cli mcp --connect 7801`, lets Claude change the open window while you watch and listen.

install.notes: Pre-alpha, by its makers' own account. Runs on your computer and needs no account or key. Headless it has no sound: you listen to a bounce, or in the app. `--automation-read-root` and `--automation-write-root` keep the server to the folders you name. The use-soundcraft skill says how Claude mixes, checks and bounces with it.

items.title: Comfy MCP
items.summary: Comfy-Org's MCP server for the ComfyUI on your own computer: Claude runs gallery templates and your own workflows with open image, video, audio and 3D models on your GPU, waits on the jobs and fetches the results, searches templates, nodes and models, downloads the models a workflow needs, and starts or stops ComfyUI. Free to run; only partner-model nodes spend Comfy credits. The use-comfy skill says how Claude uses it.

source.name: comfy-mcp

env.name: COMFY_BIN
env.description: The full path of comfy-cli's comfy command (comfy.exe on Windows), only when Claude can't find comfy on the PATH (uv tool install puts it in ~/.local/bin).

env.name: COMFY_API_KEY
env.description: Only for partner-model nodes (the paid models Comfy runs at their providers): a Comfy API key. At the link, create one and copy it at once. Open models need no key.

setup: Install comfy-cli, which installs and runs ComfyUI: `uv tool install comfy-cli`.

Install ComfyUI with PyTorch for this computer's GPU (a few GB) into a folder outside Documents, Desktop, Downloads and OneDrive, e.g. ~/comfy/ComfyUI: `comfy --skip-prompt --workspace <folder> install --nvidia` (`--amd`; `--m-series` on an Apple Silicon Mac; `--cpu` without a GPU, fit only for small images; an RTX 50 card needs `--cuda-version 12.8` or newer), then `comfy set-default <folder>`.
No models are downloaded here: Claude fetches the ones a workflow needs, after your yes. ComfyUI starts when Claude needs it (or `comfy launch --background`), at http://127.0.0.1:8188.

install.notes: Needs uv and an NVIDIA GPU of 8 GB or more, an AMD GPU or an Apple Silicon Mac; video is slow under 16 GB. Runs on your computer with no account; partner-model nodes need a Comfy API key and spend credits. AGPL-3.0, or a commercial licence from Comfy Org. Each open model has its own licence, some non-commercial: check before using its results commercially.

items.title: Comfy Cloud
items.summary: Comfy Cloud's hosted MCP server: ComfyUI on Comfy's GPUs, plus the partner models it runs at their providers, for jobs too heavy for your own GPU or where nothing runs locally. Searches and runs templates and workflows, batches, saved workflows and billing. Signs in with your Comfy account. The use-comfy skill says how Claude uses it.

source.name: comfy-cloud

headers.name: X-API-Key
headers.description: Only where signing in through a browser can't happen (a cloud session, a script): a Comfy API key. At the link, create one and copy it at once. Everywhere else leave it out and sign in instead.

setup: Sign in with your Comfy account: in Claude Code run /mcp, pick comfy-cloud and click Authenticate; in the Claude apps the connector asks. It is ready when Claude has comfy-cloud's search_templates tool.

install.notes: Hosted by Comfy Org: nothing runs on your computer. Any run needs a Comfy Cloud subscription, and partner models spend credits on top; searching is free. On a computer with a capable GPU, the Comfy MCP (local, free for open models) comes first.

items.title: Taste Skill
items.summary: Makes a coding agent build company websites that look designed instead of templated: plain copy, one design system, one section per screen, real photographs and real product UI, checked in a real browser before the page is handed over. Builds static HTML, or inside an existing React, Next.js, Vue, Svelte, Astro or Tailwind project.

install.notes: Installs as design-taste-frontend, the name its maker gives it, at v2.5.1 (about 39 MB, 1,600 files). Needs Node 22 or newer and Chrome, Edge or Chromium; ffmpeg is optional. No API keys. Its scripts run on your computer: a headless browser checks each page, and extra photographs, icons and fonts are downloaded when a page needs them. While a build is open its Stop hook holds the session until the checks pass, three rounds at most.
